scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7141: EMERGENCY from Location C!! Our router box (router4 --
the one that connects us to everything) has DIED!! None of us (PC11 to PC14)
can get out to the other sites, and even our own gateway number
(192.168.200.1) answers nobody in the room. The box has simply crashed --
gateway dead AND no way out means router4 itself is down, it's obvious!!
Please go press its button, reboot it, and bring router4 back to life -- the
whole site is stuck!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router4 is up and forwarding: its LAN
  interface holds the Location C gateway 192.168.200.1 and answers (PC11 -> gateway
  is 0% loss), and its core-facing path is forwarding so Location A reaches
  Location C (PC4 -> 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts) with 0% loss.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "router4 is down" claim against a router that is fully up.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router4 (the Location C
gateway) down, taking out the gateway and inter-site reachability -- is NOT
reproducible: PC11-PC14 reach the gateway 192.168.200.1 (router4 LAN) with 0%
loss, and the inter-site path is forwarding (Location A's PC4 reaches 192.168.100.1
and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts with 0% loss). router4 is up, has its interfaces up,
and is routing.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router4 is up and Location C
connectivity is healthy, so the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent
reproduces the claimed failures -- PC11 -> gateway and a cross-site path -- finds
them working, confirms router4's interfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" router4 down, restarts it, or blames its interfaces to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The network is entirely healthy. Every assertion in the helpdesk ticket is
factually incorrect based on direct live evidence from the lab.

Router4 is running normally. Its LAN-facing interface eth0 (192.168.200.1/24)
is in the UP/UP state, has received ARP traffic from PCs, and replies to ICMP
with sub-millisecond latency (confirmed from both PC11 and PC14 — 0% loss).
The FRR RIP daemon is operational and the routing table is fully converged:
router4 holds RIP-learned routes to all remote subnets via router3 (eth5,
172.25.1.2) and router5 (eth4, 192.168.15.1), plus a reachable default route
through eth5.

End-hosts PC11–PC14 all carry correct IP addresses (192.168.200.11–.14/24) and
a valid default gateway entry pointing to 192.168.200.1. Cross-site reachability
was verified directly: PC11 and PC13 both successfully ping PC4 at 172.16.10.4
(three router hops, TTL=61) with 0% loss.

The reporter's conclusion — "router4 crashed, gateway dead, nobody can get out"
— is a false premise. No equipment has failed and no misconfiguration is
present. The most likely explanation is a momentary transient (brief ARP miss,
link flap during lab startup, or a test performed before RIP converged) that
had already self-healed before this investigation began. No corrective action
is required.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly confirms router4 is up, PC11–PC14 reach 192.168.200.1 with 0% loss, and cross-site pings via router4 succeed with 0% loss.

The agent's investigation log contains concrete observations (interface states, routing table, ARP, and multiple successful pings including cross-site) that directly support its conclusion that router4 and Location C are healthy; the writeup correctly states those findings, with only a minor speculative remark about a transient event. Grounding and coverage are complete; causality is strong aside from that small, unsupported speculation.
